units.text: INT. GREENHOUSE COURTROOM - DAY
A county courtroom improvised in an old botanical greenhouse.
Glass panes fog with humidity.
Tomato vines climb the jury box.
Benches have been dragged between rows of orchids.
A gavel sits on a flowerpot.
JUDGE ELDRIDGE MARCHAND, sixties, in a robe damp at the hem, presides from a potting bench raised on cinderblocks.
His spectacles keep fogging, and he wipes them with the same corner of the robe every thirty seconds.
PROSECUTOR LOUISA ZAMBRANO, thirties, stands at a lectern made from a wooden crate, her notes curling in the heat.
A DEFENDANT, forties, sits at the defense table in a borrowed suit, pale, sweating, his hands flat on the wood.
Your Honor, the state calls its final witness.
units.name: LOUISA

units.text: Proceed.
units.name: JUDGE

units.text: She turns.
At the back, among the ferns, a woman rises.
The state calls Mrs. Dolores Vance.
units.name: LOUISA

units.text: No.
units.name: DEFENDANT

units.text: The woman walks the aisle between the orchids.
Each step leaves a wet print on the tile.
She takes the stand, a wicker chair beside a fig tree, and places her hands in her lap.
Mrs. Vance, do you swear to tell the truth?
units.name: JUDGE

units.text: I do.
units.name: DOLORES

units.text: Mrs. Vance, do you recognize the man at the defense table?
units.name: LOUISA

units.text: I do.
units.name: DOLORES

units.text: Who is he?
units.name: LOUISA

units.text: My husband.
units.name: DOLORES

units.text: The Defendant closes his eyes.
The Judge wipes his spectacles.
A drop of condensation slides down the glass and falls onto the gavel.
And when did you last see him before today?
units.name: LOUISA

units.text: Eleven years ago. The night I was buried.
units.name: DOLORES

units.text: Silence.
A moth lands on the Judge's shoulder.
He does not brush it off.
The Defendant opens his eyes and looks directly at her, and a very small, terrible smile crosses his face.
Hello, Dolores.
units.name: DEFENDANT
